title: Toronto Midnight Madness Title ‘Vintage Violence,’ Starring Cole Sprouse and Kiko Mizuhara, Boarded by Best Friend Forever (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Best Friend Forever has boarded international sales on Eugene Kotlyarenko’s “Vintage Violence,” starring Cole Sprouse (“Riverdale”) and Kiko Mizuhar
body:
Best Friend Forever has boarded international sales on Eugene Kotlyarenko’s “Vintage Violence,” starring Cole Sprouse (“Riverdale”) and Kiko Mizuhara, ahead of the film’s world premiere at Toronto’s Midnight Madness section.

	WME is handling domestic rights on the thriller, which marks Kotlyarenko’s eighth feature. The filmmaker is known for weaving internet and online-video culture into contemporary stories, most notably with “Spree,” which premiered at Sundance in 2020 and later reached Netflix’s Top 10, and “The Code,” which played at Fantasia in 2024.
	

	“Vintage Violence” also stars Nijiro Murakami (“Alice in Borderland”), Pierre Taki (“Like Father Like Son”) and Hio Miyazawa (“Egoist”). Mizuhara, who leads the cast with Sprouse, will also appear in Takashi Miike’s untitled Kyoto film.


	The film follows a livestreamer who discovers a hidden cache of rare vintage denim in Colorado. After a subscriber lures him to Japan with the promise of a fortune for the jeans, he becomes embroiled in a dangerous turf war with the Yakuza.

	The key crew includes Sean Price Williams, the topnotch cinematographer of “Good Time,” “The Sweet East” and “The Moment,” among others. 

	“‘Vintage Violence’ was made with lots of enthusiasm and cinephilia from everyone involved, so it’s great to work with Best Friend Forever, a company brimming with both those qualities,” said Kotlyarenko said. “Most importantly, we have the same goal in mind: for audiences all over the world to get rocked by this movie.”

	The film reteams Kotlyarenko with producers Alex Hughes and Riccardo Maddalosso of Spacemaker Productions, which also backed ’s “Spree” and “The Code.” The company’s credits also include James Gray’s “Armageddon Time” and Sebastián Silva’s “Rotting in the Sun,” among others. Japan’s Barravento, whose credits include “Onoda: 10,000 Nights in the Jungle,” and Mam Film, behind “Love Life,” are co-producing.
	

	“We’re huge fans of Eugene’s cinema and the unique way he turns our hyper-connected moment into a playful, fresh cinematic language,” said Best Friend Forever co-founders Martin Gondre and Charles Bin. “‘Vintage Violence’ feels like an exciting new step – a funny, romantic and irreverent thriller, made with a freedom of style that recalls Takashi Miike,” they continued. 

	“Vintage Violence” joins Best Friend Forever’s fall 2026 slate, which also includes the Toronto titles “Half” and Cannes Un Certain Regard Jury Prize winner “Elephants in the Fog.”

schema.headline: Toronto Midnight Madness Title ‘Vintage Violence,’ Starring Cole Sprouse and Kiko Mizuhara, Boarded by Best Friend Forever (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Brad Pitt’s ‘Heart of the Beast’ Added to San Sebastián Lineup
description: Paramount Pictures’ “The Heart of the Beast,” starring Brad Pitt and directed by David Ayer, has been added to San Sebastián Film Festival’s lineup,
body:
Paramount Pictures’ “The Heart of the Beast,” starring Brad Pitt and directed by David Ayer, has been added to San Sebastián Film Festival’s lineup, screening out of competition in its Official Selection.

	Both Pitt and Ayer will attend San Sebastián to present the film, the Spanish film festival announced Monday. 

	The survival thriller sees Pitt, a former Army Special Forces soldier, who must find a way back to civilization after his small plane crashes deep in the Alaskan wilderness. 
	

	Aided by a retired service dog, Odin, who protects him from bears, wolves and other beasts, Pitt’s character must battle the elements and embark on a desperate attempt to stay alive, climb mountains and cross rivers.


	Academy Award winner J.K. Simmons and Anna Lambe star with Pitt, who serves as a producer with Olivia Hamilton and Marty Bowen alongside Ayer.“Heart of the Beast” was written by Cameron Alexander and executive produced by Alexander, Damien Chazelle, Scott Lumpkin, Chris Long, Pete Chiappetta, Anthony Tittanegro, Andrew Lary, Sophie Cassidy and Zack Conroy.

	A Wild Chickens, Temple Hill, and Kino World production, the thriller was created in association with Domain Entertainment and Gulfstream Pictures.

	Reuniting Pitt and Ayer after “Fury,” their 2014 World War II epic for Sony, “Heart of the Beast” marks the first announcement of big star presence at this year’s San Sebastián, which runs Sept. 18-26. 

	Another big name is likely to be Penelope Cruz, star of Olivia Wilde’s “The Invite,” who also makes an extended cameo as a cabaret singer rousing the troops in Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s “La bola negra.” Both films are selected for San Sebastián’s best-of-fests Perlak sidebar.

schema.headline: Brad Pitt’s ‘Heart of the Beast’ Added to San Sebastián Lineup

title: Vietnamese Found-Footage Horror Hit ‘Lau Chu Hoa: The Deadliest Mansion’ Heads to North American Theaters (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Vietnamese found-footage horror film “Lầu Chú Hoả: The Deadliest Mansion” is opening in North American theaters on Sept. 4, with Mockingbird Picture
body:
Vietnamese found-footage horror film “Lầu Chú Hoả: The Deadliest Mansion” is opening in North American theaters on Sept. 4, with Mockingbird Pictures placing the title across AMC, Regal and Cinemark circuits.

	Directed by Hùng Trần, the film became Vietnam‘s first theatrical found-footage horror release and turned into a breakout hit after its June debut. It topped the local box office, drew more than one million admissions and crossed VND78 billion ($3 million) in cumulative grosses.
	

	The story pulls from a well-known Vietnamese urban legend: a band of young streamers force their way into the notoriously haunted Hứa family estate, hoping the stunt will bring them fame and money. Instead their broadcast captures a dormant, malevolent force stirring back to life, pulling them into the century-old tale of the “Ghost of the Hứa Family.” The entire film was shot in found-footage style.


	“Lầu Chú Hoả: The Deadliest Mansion” was produced by Runup Vietnam alongside South Korea’s Hive Media Corp, marking the Korean company’s first production investment outside its home market. Hive has backed several of Korea’s biggest recent releases, including “12.12: The Day,” “Inside Men,” “The Man Standing Next” and “Harbin,” along with the found-footage horror title “Gonjiam: Haunted Asylum,” which drew more than 2.6 million admissions in South Korea.

	“Found footage has the power to make audiences feel as though they are experiencing the horror themselves,” said producer Lee Jin Sung. “Working with Hive Media Corp allowed us to bring that experience to a uniquely Vietnamese legend while preserving the identity and atmosphere that make the story distinctive.”
	

	Mockingbird Pictures is overseeing the North American theatrical rollout as part of its broader effort to bring Vietnamese commercial films to international audiences.

	“‘Lầu Chú Hoả: The Deadliest Mansion’ delivers one of the most intense Vietnamese horror experiences in recent years,” said Phong Duong, business director of Mockingbird Pictures and one of the executive producers at sister company Bluebells Studios. “We believe this is a film that can travel, and we want audiences around the world to experience that fear for themselves.”

	Mockingbird Pictures’ distribution footprint spans more than 60 new theatrical releases a year in Vietnam and upwards of 100 titles across post-theatrical platforms, reflecting the company’s growing focus on bringing Southeast Asian films to international audiences.

schema.headline: Vietnamese Found-Footage Horror Hit ‘Lau Chu Hoa: The Deadliest Mansion’ Heads to North American Theaters (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘EastEnders’ Puts Out Casting Call for Character Named Meghan After Duchess’ U.K. Return: ‘Confident, Gorgeous and Ready to Cause Chaos’
description: Reports of Meghan Markle’s return to acting in the U.K. prompted numerous quips and memes over the weekend that the Duchess of Sussex was planning t
body:
Reports of Meghan Markle’s return to acting in the U.K. prompted numerous quips and memes over the weekend that the Duchess of Sussex was planning to make an appearance on long-running BBC soap “EastEnders.”

	Now it seems “EastEnders” producers have gotten in on the joke, as BBC Studios have put out a casting call for a new series regular called “Meghan” who they describe as “confident, gorgeous and ready to cause chaos.”
	

	A member of the newly-arrived Hawkins family, “Meghan” will work as a “senior member of the team behind a bar” – presumably the show’s iconic pub, The Old Vic, whose indomitable landladies have included Peggy Mitchell (Barbara Windsor) and Pat Butcher (Pam St Clement).


	The casting call, which is looking for a female aged around 30 years old, describes the character’s arrival into Albert Square akin to “an Essex bombshell walking into the ‘Love Island’ villa” and describes her as “funny, fearless and fiercely loyal.”

	“Quick-witted and impossible to intimidate, Meghan never backs down from a confrontation, she has spent her whole life proving she can handle whatever is thrown at her,” the breakdown reads.

	“Meghan knows what she wants in life and has never relied on anyone else to get by. She’s worked every job imaginable over the years, grafting hard to build a life for herself and earning every penny she’s made… a trait that has made her family very proud of her.”

	While “Meghan” can be “warm, charismatic, effortlessly charming,” those who cross her beware, because she’s “equally capable of throwing someone out on their ear if they cross a line.”
	

	Meghan will be part of the Hawkins family, the majority of whom arrived on Albert Square last week. Introduced as the estranged family of Nicola Mitchell, they include Gemma (Patricia Potter), husband Ned (Jamie Bamber) and son Ryder (Felix Uff). Meghan is Gemma’s daughter.

	Meghan’s isn’t the first royal presence on the long-running BBC soap, albeit in a fictional form. Her father-in-law King Charles and Queen Camilla made a surprise cameo on the show in 2022, interacting with residents during a Platinum Jubilee street party. King Charles’ mother Queen Elizabeth II also visited the set in 2001, although she did not cameo in an episode.

	For actors interested in throwing their hat in the ring, the casting call closes Sept. 1.

schema.headline: ‘EastEnders’ Puts Out Casting Call for Character Named Meghan After Duchess’ U.K. Return: ‘Confident, Gorgeous and Ready to Cause Chaos’

title: Venice Adds ‘Naza,’ Documentary From ‘No Other Land’ Directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, to Competition
description: The Venice Film Festival has made a last-minute addition to its competition lineup: “Naza,” a new documentary from “No Other Land” directors Yuval A
body:
The Venice Film Festival has made a last-minute addition to its competition lineup: “Naza,” a new documentary from “No Other Land” directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor. 

	The doc, which was shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, shows “in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza,” according to its official synopsis. 

	“Naza” is produced by The Guardian and James Wilson of JW Films, and executive produced by Jonathan Glazer. Wilson and Glazer also worked on 2023’s “The Zone of Interest” together, which won the Oscar for best international feature. 
	

	Abraham and Szor are two of the four co-directors of 2025’s Oscar-winning doc “No Other Land.” That film, which premiered at Berlin Film Festival, showed the destruction and displacement of Masafer Yatta, a Palestinian community in the West Bank. 


	“Naza” will screen at Venice Film Festival on Sept. 10 at 5:15 p.m. in the Sala Grande at the Palazzo del Cinema, in the presence of the directors, producers, Guardian journalists and the official delegation. 

	The film is the only documentary included in this year’s Venice competition section. It joins a starry lineup including Lance Oppenheim’s “Primetime,” Danny Boyle’s “Ink,” Casey Affleck’s “Company,” Werner Herzog’s “Bucking Fastard,” Hirokazu Kore-eda’s “Look Back,” Martin McDonagh’s “Wild Horse Nine,” Florian Zeller’s “Bunker” and more. It marks Abraham and Szor’s first time competing for Venice’s Golden Lion, which will be awarded at the closing ceremony on Sept. 12. 

	The 83rd edition of the Venice Film Festival kicks off Sept. 2.

schema.headline: Venice Adds ‘Naza,’ Documentary From ‘No Other Land’ Directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, to Competition

title: ‘Emomee,’ Indian Kids Life-Skills Series, Lands on Netflix (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
An Indian children’s entertainment company has brought its debut original animated series to Netflix.

	“Emomee: Big Skills for Little Ones, Minis,”
body:
An Indian children’s entertainment company has brought its debut original animated series to Netflix.

	“Emomee: Big Skills for Little Ones, Minis,” from the Mumbai-based brand Emomee, features 20 episodes of some 11 minutes each, centered on characters E, Mo and Mee as they navigate everyday adventures designed to build confidence, curiosity, kindness, emotional intelligence and problem-solving in preschool-age viewers.


	“This launch represents much more than a new distribution platform. It is another milestone in building Emomee into a global entertainment company. Every step we’ve taken – from growing a loyal audience to expanding onto streaming platforms – is helping us build a long-term franchise that will extend beyond content into consumer products, licensing and live experiences,” said Pooja Jauhari, founder and CEO of Emomee.
	

	Founded by Jauhari, a former CEO of WPP-acquired creative agency The Glitch, and Varun Duggirala, co-founder of The Glitch, Emomee reached one billion views across more than 100 countries and built a subscriber base of 2.5 million within 15 months of launch. The company drew further attention on “Shark Tank India,” where all five sharks made offers at the founders’ asking valuation of INR50 crore ($5.2 million). Suraksha Subramaniam rounds out the founding team, overseeing legal and IP compliance.

	Emomee has positioned itself around what it describes as a “life-skills-first” approach to children’s content, in contrast to the algorithm-driven, high-stimulation formats that have drawn scrutiny from parents and educators globally. 
	

	The Netflix debut is part of a broader expansion push that spans consumer products, licensing and live experiences. Emomee plans to attend Mipcom later this year to pursue new deals across distribution and licensing.

title: Alia Bhatt’s Young-Adult Rom-Com ‘Don’t Be Shy’ Sets September Prime Video Premiere (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Prime Video has set a September premiere date for “Don’t Be Shy,” a young-adult romantic comedy from Alia Bhatt and Shaheen Bhatt’s Eternal Sunshine
body:
Prime Video has set a September premiere date for “Don’t Be Shy,” a young-adult romantic comedy from Alia Bhatt and Shaheen Bhatt’s Eternal Sunshine Productions.

	Sreeti Mukerji wrote and directed the coming-of-age film, which is produced by Bhatt and Shaheen Bhatt under the Eternal Sunshine Productions banner, with Grishma Shah and Vikesh Bhutani serving as co-producers.

	The film introduces four newcomers – Aarushi Bajaj, Ansh Duggal, Bianca Arora and Piyush Khati – who headline a story centered on friendship, young love, heartbreak and the process of figuring out life as a young adult. Kunaal Roy Kapur, Anurag Basu, Neha Dhupia and Anju Alva Naik round out the cast in pivotal roles.
	

	“‘Don’t Be Shy’ is one of our most cherished films, and we’re thrilled to finally announce its global streaming premiere,” said Nikhil Madhok, director and head of originals, Prime Video (SVOD) and Amazon MGM Studios India. “This film introduces four extraordinary new actors – Aarushi, Ansh, Bianca, and Piyush – who bring an incredible freshness and authenticity to their roles. Led by Sreeti Mukerji and shaped by the creative vision of Alia and Shaheen Bhatt, ‘Don’t Be Shy’ is a joyful, heartfelt celebration of friendship, love, and the beautifully messy journey of growing up. We can’t wait for audiences to immerse themselves in Shy’s world.”


	Alia Bhatt and Shaheen Bhatt, co-founders of Eternal Sunshine Productions, added in a joint statement: “‘Don’t Be Shy’ has been extremely special to us from the very beginning, and we couldn’t be prouder to see it come to life. It captures something so honest about being young – the friendships that shape you, the first loves that change you, the heartbreaks that stay with you, and the process of gradually figuring out who you are. What excites us most is this brilliant young cast; their energy, vulnerability, and chemistry are magnetic, and they bring such life and honesty to these characters. We can’t wait for audiences in India and around the world to meet Shy and get swept into her wonderful, chaotic world.” 
	

	Eternal Sunshine Productions was founded in 2021 by Bhatt, one of the most celebrated actors in Indian cinema, and her sister Shaheen Bhatt, author of the mental health memoir “I’ve Never Been (Un)Happier” (Penguin Ebury Press, 2019). The company’s debut feature, “Darlings,” bowed in August 2022 as a Red Chillies co-production and marked Jasmeet K. Reen’s feature directorial debut. Eternal Sunshine’s slate also includes “Poacher,” the Prime Video series from Emmy winner Richie Mehta, and “Jigra,” an action-adventure from Vasan Bala co-produced with Dharma Productions.

	“Don’t Be Shy” will premiere exclusively on Prime Video in Hindi with English subtitles across India and more than 240 countries and territories worldwide on Sept. 25.

schema.headline: Alia Bhatt’s Young-Adult Rom-Com ‘Don’t Be Shy’ Sets September Prime Video Premiere (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘An Oak Tree’ Casts Sacha Dhawan, Gemma Whelan for London Run (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Francesca Moody Productions has unveiled the first wave of guest performers joining Tim Crouch’s “An Oak Tree” for its run at The Other Palace in Lo
body:
Francesca Moody Productions has unveiled the first wave of guest performers joining Tim Crouch’s “An Oak Tree” for its run at The Other Palace in London, with Sacha Dhawan, Gemma Whelan, Bessie Carter, Rosalie Craig, Hammed Animashaun, George Fouracres, Clare Perkins and Tom Mothersdale each taking on a single performance.

	Crouch performs alongside a different second actor at every show, none of whom read or rehearse the script in advance. “An Oak Tree” runs at The Other Palace from Oct. 7 through Nov. 15.
	

	The schedule of guest performers, in order, runs as follows: Craig on Oct. 9, Perkins on Oct. 13, Mothersdale on Oct. 14, Whelan on Oct. 15, Carter on Oct. 16, Dhawan on Oct. 23, Animashaun on Oct. 29 and Fouracres on Nov. 10.


	Craig recently starred as Kitty Eckersley in Sally Wainwright’s “Riot Women” for BBC One and earned an Olivier nomination for “The Light Princess” at the National Theatre. Perkins appeared in Indhu Rubasingham’s “Bacchae” at the National Theatre and starred opposite Sadie Sink in “Romeo & Juliet” in the West End. Mothersdale’s stage credits include “A Doll’s House” and “Oil” at the Almeida Theatre, while his television work spans “Wolf Hall: The Mirror and the Light” and “Peaky Blinders.”

	Whelan is known for playing Yara Greyjoy in HBO’s “Game of Thrones” and has appeared across all three series of ITV’s “The Tower.” Carter currently plays Nancy Mitford in BritBox’s “Outrageous” and is also known for playing Prudence Featherington in Netflix’s “Bridgerton.” Dhawan has been announced for Netflix’s “Extraction” and plays the latest incarnation of the Master in BBC One’s “Doctor Who.” Animashaun, a BAFTA nominee for “Black Ops,” appeared in Sky’s “SNL U.K.” and the Donmar Warehouse’s “Dealer’s Choice.” Fouracres, another “SNL U.K.” cast member, is a regular at Shakespeare’s Globe, with credits including “Hamlet” and “Twelfth Night.”
	

	“An Oak Tree” premiered in 2005 and has since been performed hundreds of times across more than 19 countries, with more than 350 guest artists taking part over two decades. Past performers include Frances McDormand, Geoffrey Rush, Peter Dinklage, David Tennant, Jessie Buckley and Phoebe Waller-Bridge.

	The production is part of a new Francesca Moody Productions season at The Other Palace running from Oct. 5, 2026 through Jan. 10, 2027, bringing together three shows that originated at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe. The season also includes “Garry Starr: Classic Penguins,” created by Damien Warren-Smith and running Oct. 22 through Jan. 3 with a press night of Oct. 23, and “Feeling Afraid As If Something Terrible Is Going to Happen,” written by Marcelo Dos Santos and starring Steven Webb, running Nov. 19 through Jan. 10.

	Francesca Moody, the season’s executive producer, originated two of the past decade’s most successful television adaptations, “Fleabag” and “Baby Reindeer,” both of which began as stage productions before moving to the screen.

schema.headline: ‘An Oak Tree’ Casts Sacha Dhawan, Gemma Whelan for London Run (EXCLUSIVE)

title: California Attorney General Cancels Paramount Settlement Talks Over $111 Billion Warner Bros. Discovery Deal, Says He’ll Meet When They ‘Stop Playing Games’
description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta has canceled planned settlement talks with Paramount over the state’s lawsuit seeking to block David Ellison‘s
body:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta has canceled planned settlement talks with Paramount over the state’s lawsuit seeking to block David Ellison‘s proposed $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, accusing Paramount of acting in bad faith, according to The New York Times. 

	Bonta is leading a coalition of 12 states in challenging the proposed merger and asking the court to block the deal, arguing the merger would give the company too much power across cable television and movie production. 
	

	The two sides had been due to meet Monday for preliminary discussions for a possible settlement, but Bonta called off the meeting late Sunday, after accusing Paramount of misrepresenting details of an earlier meeting held on Friday. 


	“Not only did Paramount leak the alleged substance of settlement discussions, but they misrepresented these discussions, demonstrating a lack of good faith,” Bonta said in a statement sent to The New York Times. “As soon as Paramount stops playing games and engages sincerely, my office is happy to meet again.” 

	Variety has reached out to the California AG office for comment. 

	The canceled meeting had been perceived as a possible opening toward  resolving the case, particularly after Paramount threatened to leave California. Bonta has so far insisted that any settlement would require “structural remedies,” likely involving asset sales, which Paramount may resist. 

	Pressure to resolve the dispute is growing ahead of the antitrust trial scheduled for March. As Variety previously reported, Paramount will begin accruing a “ticking fee” owed to shareholders amounting to about $7 million per day starting Oct. 1 if the deal has not closed.

schema.headline: California Attorney General Cancels Paramount Settlement Talks Over $111 Billion Warner Bros. Discovery Deal, Says He’ll Meet When They ‘Stop Playing Games’

title: Joachim Trier’s ‘Sentimental Value,’ Hlynur Pálmason’s ‘The Love That Remains’ Among the Nominees for the Nordic Council Film Prize
description: Five features and one documentary have been nominated for the 2026 Nordic Council Film Prize. It’s awarded to a feature film or documentary produced
body:
Five features and one documentary have been nominated for the 2026 Nordic Council Film Prize. It’s awarded to a feature film or documentary produced in the Nordic countries that has been distributed in cinemas.

	Some picks – announced at the Norwegian International Film Festival Haugesund – come as no surprise, as Joachim Trier’s Oscar-winning “Sentimental Value” and Hlynur Pálmason’s “The Love That Remains” have already enjoyed significant festival success. 
	

	However, the jury consisting of Jacob Ludvigsen, Jan Berg Jørgensen, Marjo Pipinen, Jóna Finnsdóttir, Anne Gjelsvik and Jonas Holmberg also recognized Jeanette Nordahl’s “Beginnings,” Búi Dam’s “Birita,” “A Light That Never Goes Out” by Lauri-Matti Parppei and “Kevlar Soul” directed by Maria Eriksson-Hecht.


	“Kevlar Soul” focuses on two brothers who grow up terrorized by their alcoholic father. 

	“We are deeply honored by this nomination,” said Eriksson-Hecht.

	“Being selected as Sweden’s entry for the Nordic Council Film Prize means a great deal to everyone involved, both in front of and behind the camera. We hope this recognition will help more people discover and see the film, bringing new attention to its themes.” 

	“Beginnings,” starring Trine Dyrholm and David Dencik, follows a couple that’s about to divorce – until Ane suffers a stroke.

	“We wanted to explore the absolute loss of control, seen from all perspectives within a family. What happens when illness strikes, and how do we relate to each other when everything has changed?,” noted Nordahl, deciding to tell the story “without sentimentality or judgement, focusing on simple, everyday situations that might feel familiar.” 
	

	“So many families find themselves in this type of conflict, and our intention was to give them a film in which they could feel seen and validated. I think, and hope, this is why audiences have responded so strongly to it.”

	In “Birita,” the only doc in the selection, Búi Dam decided to go personal.

	“Making this film about my mother, an actress, and my relationship with her has been a journey of joy, love, and discovery. And, clichéd as it may sound, that has of course been the reward in itself,” he said. But the nomination is important for another reason as well. 

	“The Faroe Islands, a semi-autonomous part of the Danish realm, have long stood on the periphery of the Nordic community. Now, as we move towards independence – something that our Icelandic sister Björk encouraged us and Greenland to do in 2008 [in her song ‘Declare Independence’] – it feels important that we carve out a clear place for our own voice, our language, and our culture within the Nordic community.”

	He added: “In that sense, this film is rebellious – just like my mother.”

	Or like the protagonists of the music-heavy drama “A Light That Never Goes Out” by Lauri-Matti Parppei, who decide to start an experimental band, aka a “paramilitary noise art collective.”  The film, which premiered at Cannes ACID, was a big winner at the Jussi Awards in its native Finland. 

	“My background is in the Finnish underground and DIY music scene. I never expected that a film based on those experiences would suddenly touch people around the world. And travel across borders and continents,” Parppei told Variety. 

	“As a Finn, I’ve always admired Nordic filmmakers and their long history of acclaimed cinema, even feeling a bit inferior. Even my favorite film of all time is from Sweden: ‘Fucking Åmål’ by Lukas Moodysson [also known as ‘Show Me Love’]. That’s why it means so much to me to be nominated alongside the works of my colleagues – and it feels like I might actually be a real Nordic filmmaker myself!”

	Greenland did not submit a film for the 2026 Nordic Council Film Prize. 

	The prize comes with 300,000 Danish kroner, which will be shared equally among the screenwriters, directors and producers to emphasize “how film as an art form is brought about by the close collaboration of these three main contributors,” it was stated. 
	

	The winners will be announced on 20 October.



	

					‘Birita’
									c: Franklin-Symphor-Henriksen-and-Outlier-Projects.
	



	Here’s the full list of the nominees:

	“Beginnings”

	Nominated director: Jeanette Nordahl

	Nominated writers: Rasmus Birch, Jeanette Nordahl

	Nominated producers: Eva Jakobsen, Katrin Pors, Mikkel Jersin

	“Birita”

	Nominated director/writer: Búi Dam

	Nominated producer: Jón Hammer, Durita Sumberg, Mark Steele

	“Kevlar Soul”

	Nominated director: Maria Eriksson-Hecht

	Nominated writers: Pelle Rådström

	Nominated producers: Ronny Fritsche, Lizette Jonjic

	“A Light That Never Goes Out”

	Nominated director/writer: Lauri-Matti Parppei

	Nominated producer: Ilona Tolmunen

	“The Love That Remains”

	Nominated director/writer: Hlynur Pálmason

	Nominated producers: Anton Máni Svansson, Katrin Pors

	“Sentimental Value”

	Nominated director: Joachim Trier

	Nominated writers: Eskil Vogt, Joachim Trier

	Nominated producers: Maria Ekerhovd, Andrea Berentsen Ottmar

                          Missing 'AGT' For Weeks ...

body:
Simon Cowell
                          Missing 'AGT' For Weeks ...
                          Due to Routine Surgery
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 23, 2026
                            8:00 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  August 24, 2026
                                5:28 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Simon Cowell is going to be missing from "America's Got Talent" for the next couple of weeks while he undergoes a routine procedure related to his back, TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Sources with direct knowledge tell TMZ ... Cowell is scheduled to have back surgery soon, and the procedure will force him to sit out several weeks of the hit NBC show.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            We're told this is a routine procedure and there is no indication of a new major health crisis. Cowell has a history of back issues following a serious electric-bike accident in 2020 that required surgery.
      

            It's unclear who will fill in for Cowell during his absence or exactly when he'll return to the judges' table.
      
    
            The 66-year-old British music mogul and TV personality is best known for his brutally honest judging style on "American Idol," "The X Factor" and "America’s Got Talent."
      
    
            Cowell has also been instrumental in creating and developing major acts including One Direction and Fifth Harmony, cementing his reputation as one of pop music’s most influential talent scouts.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            We recently caught up with Cowell in March, when he weighed in on Tom Sandoval and his band ... saying he didn’t see them as major record sellers but thought they could make serious money playing weddings and parties.
      
    
            Cowell also revealed to us he’s considering putting together another boy or girl group, saying he’s still looking for the next big act.
      
    
            We’ve reached out to Crowell’s reps for comment. So far, no word back.

title: President Trump Claims Biden Officials Drove People to Suicide
description:
President Trump
                          Blames Biden Admin for 'Many Suicides'
body:
President Trump
                          Blames Biden Admin for 'Many Suicides'
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                August 23, 2026
                
                            4:45 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  August 23, 2026
                                5:41 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Donald Trump is making a shocking claim about his political enemies ... alleging people committed suicide over the way they were treated by Joe Biden's administration.
      
    
            POTUS dropped the claim during his full WABC interview with former fixer-turned-foe-turned-friend Michael Cohen Sunday ... but didn't identify who he was talking about or offer evidence to support it.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Trump said, "We had many suicides, people committed suicide over this" ... before blaming what he called vicious people in the Biden administration -- and taking a swipe at Barack Obama's administration, too.
      

            He then turned his fire on former government officials who've since landed jobs in the private sector and media ... claiming some now work at Microsoft and others appear on CNN.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Trump specifically went after former FBI personnel who became TV commentators ... calling them "FBI slobs" and accusing them of being "dirty cops."
      
    
            There wasn't much context given for exactly which investigations or individuals Trump was talking about ... and he didn't name anyone he says died by suicide.
      
    
            The remarks came during Trump's newly repaired relationship with Cohen -- once his longtime personal lawyer before the two became bitter enemies.
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported ... Cohen told us last month the two were "reconciling" and putting their past aside after private meetings at Bedminster and Mar-a-Lago.
      
    
                    
                          
                                  
      
        
    
            Now they're back talking publicly ... and Trump definitely didn't hold back.
